Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: Unit 2. Routine and fun
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Let's have fun together!
- Materials: Activity cards, preference chart, weekend planner, COSYmanuals 'like/love/hate' and 'present simple' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• express group leisure preferences
• use love / like / enjoy + -ing in social contexts
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles hobbies and preference verbs from A0.

Next lesson: Lesson 8 moves to workplace collocations and office culture.

Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

music — sounds made with voices or instruments. Example: We listen to music together.
cinema — a place to watch films. Example: We go to the cinema on Friday.
football — a sport played with a ball and two teams. Example: We play football on Saturday.
gaming — playing computer games. Example: He enjoys gaming.
fun — enjoyment. Example: We have fun together.
together — with each other. Example: We eat together every evening.
enjoy — to like doing something. Example: I enjoy swimming.
love — to like something very much. Example: I love music.
like — to enjoy something. Example: I like chocolate.
hobby — an activity you enjoy in free time. Example: My hobby is reading.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Let's have fun together! (suggesting a group activity)
• I enjoy... (expressing preference)
• We love... (expressing group preference)
• Do you like...? (asking about preference)
• How about...? (making a suggestion)
• That sounds fun! (accepting a suggestion)

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'like', 'love', 'enjoy', and 'hate' to talk about preferences.

Form:
Like / love / hate + -ing: Subject + like / love / enjoy / hate + verb-ing. I like reading. She loves dancing. They hate cooking.

Examples:
• I like reading.
• She loves dancing.
• We enjoy playing football.
• He hates cooking.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
I like ___. (read)
She loves ___. (dance)
They hate ___. (cook)
We enjoy ___. (play) football.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I like ... (-ing).
• I love ... (-ing).
• I hate ... (-ing).
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What do you like doing in your free time?
• What do you hate doing?
• What does your friend love doing?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your hobbies with 'like/love/hate + -ing'.
• Write three sentences about a friend's hobbies.
Reading: Let's have fun together!

Let's have fun together! We enjoy going to the cinema and playing football. My friends love gaming, and I like listening to music. On Saturday, we usually meet at the park. We sometimes watch a film together. What do you enjoy doing? How about joining us this weekend?
What do they enjoy doing?
options: going to the cinema and playing football

elements.content: When do they usually meet?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: What do you enjoy doing?
B: I love gaming and listening to music.
A: Do you like football?
B: Yes, I do. How about playing football this weekend?
A: That sounds fun! Let's meet at the park.
What does the speaker love?
Where are they going to meet?
Speaking task: Plan a fun group activity for the weekend. Suggest three options and agree on one.

• What do you enjoy doing with friends?
• Do you like going to the cinema?
• How often do you play football or games?
• What is fun for you?
• How about trying a new hobby?
Role-play: You are planning a class outing. Suggest activities, ask for opinions, and agree on a plan.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about group leisure activities you enjoy.
Model: We enjoy ... I love ... My friends like ... How about ...?
